claim: The one-click demo loads five sample worktrees.
sandbox: fresh browser context; click the primary action; assert five sample rows

claim: Blocked agents and dirty branches appear on the board.
sandbox: fresh browser context and bundled sample data; assert blocked and changed states

claim: The sample action and its explanation are visible in the initial desktop and 390px mobile viewport.
sandbox: fresh browser context at 1440x900, 1280x800, and 390x844; measure the full action and explanation inside each viewport

claim: Demo repository data is not sent off the device or saved as real data.
sandbox: fresh browser context; intercept the full demo flow; assert same-origin requests and demo-only session storage

claim: The sample board works offline after its first visit.
sandbox: fresh browser context; load demo once; wait for service worker; set offline; reload and assert five rows

claim: Pulse scans Git metadata and three opt-in adapter fields; it ignores source, prompt, output, and terminal content without changing Git state.
where: landing facts and privacy section, native first-run screen, privacy page, README
sandbox: temporary real Git repository with source, prompt, output, and terminal canaries; run the native scan, assert no canary enters serialized board data, and compare Git and file state before and after

claim: Five worktrees are free and Pulse Pro costs $19 once.
where: landing facts, paid tier, terms, README
sandbox: fresh browser context; assert the free limit and one-time price are shown

claim: The demo works without an account.
sandbox: fresh browser context with no cookies or storage; open the one-click demo and assert the board loads

claim: Pulse Pro shows every worktree and refreshes every 10 seconds.
where: landing paid tier, native limit notice, terms, README
sandbox: eight-worktree fixture; assert free mode returns five, Pro returns all eight, and the production scheduler requests exactly 10000 milliseconds

claim: The public site contacts GitHub only after the visitor requests a release download.
sandbox: fresh browser context with request interception; assert no cross-origin landing requests, click download check, and assert only the GitHub Releases API request

claim: A returned license token stays in local storage and verification sends it only to the Sociobot billing API.
sandbox: fresh browser context with a returned fixture license and mocked Sociobot response; assert URL stripping, namespaced local storage, and the single allowed verification request

claim: The download button selects the matching Intel or Apple silicon macOS build.
sandbox: mock GitHub release with both DMGs; use Intel and Apple silicon browser fixtures; assert each direct download URL

claim: Selecting a real worktree opens a terminal in that exact worktree folder.
where: landing How it works section and README
sandbox: temporary worktree and configured terminal probe; assert the probe receives the selected folder as its working directory

claim: The one-line installers verify SHA-256 before opening or installing a release file.
sandbox: read both shipped installer scripts; assert their checksum rejection check precedes every open, copy, or process-start operation

claim: The desktop app includes no analytics or crash tracking.
sandbox: inspect native and WebView source for network clients and known analytics or crash-tracking endpoints

claim: Remove repository forgets a saved path without changing repository files.
sandbox: save two local paths, remove one through the storage action, and assert only that saved path is gone

claim: The $19 Pulse Pro purchase link opens a live Dodo checkout.
sandbox: make one live request to the advertised Sociobot checkout URL; require HTTP 303 to an HTTPS checkout.dodopayments.com session
